The test image shows a corn leaf sheath with extensive brown-tan water-soaked necrosis, darker grayish-black at the top area, and wet-looking tissue. The affected part is the leaf sheath/stalk junction area. Key features: large irregular brown lesion, wet/water-soaked appearance, dark areas at top.

Top candidates: Goss_wilt (large irregular water-soaked lesions), Bacterial_stalk_rot (leaf sheath discoloration, soft rot), Anthracnose_stalk_rot (shiny black stalk lesions).

Let me view the Goss_wilt reference to compare.

The Goss_wilt reference shows characteristic streaks along leaf veins and freckles — not matching the test image well.

**Analysis of test image:**
- Affected part: lower stalk/leaf sheath junction area
- Very large, irregular tan-brown necrosis covering the entire leaf sheath
- Dark grayish-black at the top (more advanced necrosis near a node)
- Wet, water-soaked appearance throughout
- No distinct freckles, no streaking pattern, no rust pustules

**Key differential:**
- **Bacterial_stalk_rot**: "Discoloration of leaf sheath and stalk at nodes, progressing to lesions on leaves and sheath, with internal soft slimy rot... The first and/or second internode above the soil line appears water soaked, turns tan to brown." — This matches the large water-soaked tan-brown sheath/node lesion precisely.
- Goss_wilt: requires freckles and bacterial exudate — not visible
- Anthracnose_stalk_rot: requires shiny black rind lesions, not broad sheath necrosis
- Stewarts_wilt: requires streaks along veins from flea beetle scars

The large water-soaked tan-to-brown discoloration at the leaf sheath/node area, with darker necrosis advancing toward the node, is classic **Bacterial stalk rot**.
